editorial:
Imagine you are a young governess back in the Edwardian era, taking a new job at a big, creepy estate. You quickly realize that you are not alone in the house. The vibe is very eerie and slow, making you feel like something is always watching from the shadows. It starts off as a simple job, but it turns into a nightmare as you realize the house has a dark history that refuses to stay buried. You will feel the tension build up as the main character tries to figure out why the spirits are angry and if she can even get out alive.

What really works here is the acting and the old-school scares. It does not rely on loud noises, but instead uses a creepy mood to get under your skin. Some parts might feel a bit slow if you like modern slashers, but it is perfect for a rainy night.
endingExplained: The movie ends with the big reveal that the spirits are tied to a family tragedy involving a lost child. The governess discovers that the ghosts are not trying to kill her, but are trying to warn her about the house's true evil. After a final scary confrontation, the truth comes out, and the spirits are finally able to find peace. She manages to escape the house just as the cycle of pain finally breaks.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gothic ghost stories and old-fashioned mysteries.
